entries.title: Traffic violation in Mumbai (no parking, no HSRP, triple seat, wrong side, helmet, etc.)
entries.who: Mumbai Traffic Police (Traffic Branch, Mumbai Police). Local traffic division/chowky handles action; HQ at Worli.

channels.name: Mumbai Traffic Police app
channels.how: Install the official app (Android/iOS), choose the violation (no parking, triple seat, no helmet, fancy/missing plate, wrong-side etc.), attach geo-tagged photo/video with vehicle number, submit. Verified offenders are issued an e-challan.

channels.name: Mumbai Traffic Police WhatsApp / helpline
channels.how: Send photo, location and vehicle number by WhatsApp/SMS/call. You get a complaint number to track.

channels.name: Email (escalation / HQ)
channels.how: For follow-up when no action is taken.

escalation: Quote your complaint number on the helpline/WhatsApp again.
Email Traffic HQ (addresses above) with evidence and complaint number.
Visit Traffic HQ, Worli, in person.
State grievance portal Aaple Sarkar (grievances.maharashtra.gov.in) if still ignored.
entries.evidence: Clear photo showing vehicle number plate, the no-parking sign and surroundings, date/time and location. Do not post it on social media instead of sending it to the police.

sources.t: Free Press Journal: Mumbai Traffic Police helpline 8454999999 (call/WhatsApp/SMS)
Mumbai Traffic Police App (Apple App Store)

entries.title: Traffic violation in Thane / Thane Commissionerate (no parking, no HSRP, wrong side, triple seat, tinted glass, fancy plate, double parking)
entries.who: Thane City Traffic Branch (Thane Police Commissionerate). Each area belongs to a traffic unit; the unit's own WhatsApp number takes violation photos.

channels.name: Local traffic unit WhatsApp (area-wise)
channels.how: Send photo + exact location + vehicle number to the WhatsApp number of the traffic unit that covers the area (see unit table; the app resolves the unit from the place name).

channels.name: Thane Traffic Control WhatsApp
channels.how: General traffic control WhatsApp; also used for autorickshaw complaints.

channels.name: Thane Traffic helplines
channels.how: Call before contacting officers directly.

channels.name: Nirbhay Thane (official Thane Police AI WhatsApp chatbot)
channels.how: Save the number, send 'Hi', pick Traffic Services or Report a Crime.

escalation: Email the unit's PI, e.g. Naupada: cp.thane.trnaupada@mahapolice.gov.in; other units follow cp.thane.tr<unit>@mahapolice.gov.in on the contact page.
ACP Traffic Thane / DCP Traffic: City Traffic Branch Office, Teen Hat Naka, Thane (W) 400602.
Traffic Control Room Thane: 022-25394876.
Aaple Sarkar (grievances.maharashtra.gov.in) if no reply.
entries.evidence: Photo with plate readable, location landmark, time. For several violations send separate photos.

sources.t: Saamana: Thane Police WhatsApp numbers per traffic unit
Thane Traffic Police: contact us (helplines, unit emails)
Free Press Journal: Thane traffic WhatsApp 7039003866, helplines

entries.title: E-challan: pay, check or dispute a wrong challan; fake challan links
entries.who: The traffic police that issued the challan; payment via Parivahan / MahaTraffic e-challan portal.

channels.name: Parivahan e-challan (national)
channels.how: Look up by vehicle/challan number, view photo, time and place.

channels.name: MahaTraffic e-challan (Maharashtra)
channels.how: View and pay Maharashtra traffic police challans; helpdesk for technical issues.

channels.name: Dispute
channels.how: Write to the issuing traffic unit/HQ with challan number, RC, DL, payment proof/sale papers and why it is wrong. Unpaid challans may go to a virtual Lok Adalat notice; attend or pay by the date.

escalation: Issuing unit's PI/ACP traffic
Traffic HQ (Mumbai: Worli; Thane: Teen Hat Naka)
Lok Adalat / court on the notice date
entries.warning: Scam alert: fake 'RTO/Parivahan challan' WhatsApp links circulate. Open only the portals listed here by typing the address yourself; report scams on 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in.

sources.t: Free Press Journal: fake challan link scam (Thane)

entries.title: Police: filing an FIR, police refusing to register, misconduct
entries.who: Station House Officer of the police station; above that the Superintendent of Police (in Mumbai/Thane: the Deputy Commissioner of Police of the zone); then the magistrate.

channels.name: Emergency
channels.how: Immediate danger.

channels.name: Any police station (Zero FIR)
channels.how: Under Section 173 BNSS a cognizable offence must be registered at any police station irrespective of jurisdiction; you are entitled to a free copy of the FIR.

channels.name: Nirbhay Thane (Thane city)
channels.how: WhatsApp chatbot to report incidents and get police services.

escalation: If the SHO refuses: send the substance in writing (post) to the Superintendent of Police / DCP, Section 173(4) BNSS.
If still nothing: apply to the Judicial Magistrate under Section 175(3) BNSS with a copy of the SP application and an affidavit.
Constitutional remedy: writ petition in the High Court (Article 226).
Misconduct by police: complaint to DCP/Commissioner, and Aaple Sarkar grievance portal.

sources.t: Sansa Legal: FIR, Zero FIR and refusal remedies under BNSS

entries.title: Cyber fraud, UPI/online scam, harassment online
entries.who: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (MHA) with state cyber police; helpline 1930 for financial fraud.

channels.name: Helpline (do this first for money loss)
channels.how: Call immediately so the bank can freeze the transferred amount; speed matters.

channels.name: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal
channels.how: File the complaint with screenshots, transaction IDs, URLs, phone numbers.

escalation: Also inform your bank in writing and ask for a dispute number.
If the bank does not reimburse within 30 days, RBI Ombudsman (cms.rbi.org.in).
Visit local police station / cyber police station with the acknowledgement.

sources.t: Free Press Journal: 1930 helpline and NCCRP

entries.title: Consumer complaint: defective product, refund, e-commerce, service deficiency, misleading ads
entries.who: Seller/company first; then National Consumer Helpline (mediation); then the Consumer Commission (District / State / National) under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

channels.name: National Consumer Helpline (NCH / INGRAM)
channels.how: Free pre-litigation mediation with the company. Call, WhatsApp or file online.

channels.name: Consumer Commission online filing
channels.how: File a formal complaint online (the older e-Daakhil portal has moved to e-Jagriti; use the portal the Department currently shows). Attach bills, warranty, chats, notices.

escalation: 1) Written complaint to seller/company grievance officer (keep email proof).
2) NCH 1915 / consumerhelpline.gov.in.
3) Legal notice, then District Commission (pecuniary limit commonly cited as up to ₹50 lakh; State ₹50 lakh–₹2 crore; National above ₹2 crore under the 2021 rules; verify current limits).
4) Appeal to State then National Commission.
Limitation: generally 2 years from the cause of action. Do NOT use consumer court for electricity supply disputes covered by the Electricity Act.

entries.title: Electricity: power cut, wrong bill, meter issue (MSEDCL / Mahavitaran)
entries.who: MSEDCL (Mahavitaran) for most of Maharashtra incl. Thane suburbs outside Mumbai city; in Mumbai the supplier may be Adani Electricity, Tata Power or BEST — check your bill.

channels.name: MSEDCL 24x7 helplines
channels.how: Register the complaint, note the complaint number.

escalation: Level 1: helpline/ Section office.
Level 2: Internal Grievance Redressal Cell (IGRC) at the divisional office.
Level 3: Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum (CGRF) of your zone (Schedule A application) if IGRC rejects or 2 months pass.
Level 4: Electricity Ombudsman, MERC, Mumbai (Schedule B).
Non-compliance: MERC under Sections 142/146 Electricity Act.

entries.title: Mumbai civic issues: potholes, garbage, open manholes, water, drainage, illegal construction (BMC / MCGM)
entries.who: Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) ward office (24 wards) under the Municipal Commissioner.

channels.name: BMC helpline
channels.how: IVR to operator, complaint registered on the portal.

channels.name: MyBMC MARG app / portal
channels.how: Login with mobile OTP, choose category, attach geo-tagged photo, get a complaint number.

channels.name: BMC WhatsApp chatbot
channels.how: Share location and photo.

channels.name: Open/damaged manhole WhatsApp chatbot
channels.how: Location plus photo.

channels.name: Pothole Quick Fix app
channels.how: Report potholes with photo.

escalation: Hawkers: complain to the ward office (License/Encroachment dept). Street vendors with a licence/survey registration are protected under the Street Vendors Act 2014 (Town Vending Committee), so ask whether the stall is in a notified no-hawking zone. Obstruction of the road can also go to the local police.
Ward office Assistant Commissioner (written complaint / email).
BMC Public Grievance cell.
Municipal Commissioner: mc@mcgm.gov.in.
Aaple Sarkar grievance portal (Urban Development appellate officer).

sources.t: Free Press Journal: BMC grievance channels (1916, app, WhatsApp)
Free Press Journal: BMC manhole WhatsApp chatbot

entries.title: Thane civic issues: potholes, garbage, water, drainage, air pollution, illegal construction (TMC)
entries.who: Thane Municipal Corporation (TMC), ward committee/ward office under the Municipal Commissioner.

channels.name: TMC citizen helpline
channels.how: Control room registers the complaint.

channels.name: TMC online grievance / DigiThane app
channels.how: Login on thanecity.gov.in, file complaint with ward and evidence, track by ID, reopen if unresolved.

channels.name: TMC air-pollution WhatsApp
channels.how: Photo of open waste burning, construction dust, uncovered debris transport, etc.

channels.name: TMT bus complaints
channels.how: Thane Municipal Transport helpline.

escalation: Hawkers: complain to the ward office / Encroachment (Atikraman) dept via the helpline. Licensed street vendors are protected under the Street Vendors Act 2014; ask if the spot is a notified no-hawking zone. Road obstruction can also go to the local police.
Ward office / Assistant Commissioner.
Municipal Commissioner: mc@thanecity.gov.in, 022-25336523.
Aaple Sarkar grievance portal.

sources.t: Thane Police X post: TMC helpline & email
Mumbai Live: TMC air-pollution WhatsApp helpline

entries.title: Right to Information (RTI): get information or documents from a public authority
entries.who: Public Information Officer (PIO) of the department; First Appellate Authority; then State/Central Information Commission.

channels.name: Maharashtra online RTI
channels.how: Online filing works for Maharashtra government (Mantralaya) departments only; field offices and local bodies need a written application.

channels.name: Central government RTI
channels.how: Online application and first appeal for central public authorities.

escalation: Application: fee ₹10 (Maharashtra), reply due in 30 days (48 hours if life/liberty).
First appeal to the First Appellate Authority within 30 days of reply/deadline.
Second appeal to the State Information Commission (sic.maharashtra.gov.in) or CIC (cic.gov.in) within 90 days.
Maharashtra SIC online second appeal: sic.maharashtra.gov.in/siconline.

entries.title: Complaint against any Maharashtra government office or delayed government service (Aaple Sarkar, RTS, CM helpline, CPGRAMS)
entries.who: The department's grievance/appellate officers; Maharashtra State Commission for Right to Service; for central bodies CPGRAMS.

channels.name: Aaple Sarkar grievance portal + CM helpline
channels.how: Post a grievance, get a token, track; reopen to reach appellate officers.

channels.name: Aaple Sarkar RTS portal
channels.how: Apply for notified services within fixed time limits; appeal if missed.

channels.name: CPGRAMS (central govt)
channels.how: Grievances against central ministries (incl. Railways, banks' public sector arms).

escalation: RTS Act: First appeal, second appeal, then third appeal to the State Commission for Right to Service within 60 days of the second order; officer penalty up to ₹5,000 per case.
Grievance portal: first appeal officer, second appeal officer (divisional commissioner/HOD), then CMO.

sources.t: Anantam: Aaple Sarkar and RTS appeals
Complaint Hub: Aaple Sarkar grievance levels

entries.title: Bank / NBFC / UPI wallet complaint
entries.who: The bank's grievance officer first; then RBI Integrated Ombudsman.

channels.name: RBI Complaint Management System
channels.how: Complain to the bank/NBFC in writing first and wait 30 days (or rejection), then file free of cost online, by email or post.

escalation: Branch → Principal Nodal Officer of the bank.
RBI Ombudsman after 30 days / rejection (time limit stated in the current Integrated Ombudsman Scheme; recent text says 90 days, older 1 year, verify).
Appeal against Ombudsman decision within 30 days to the Appellate Authority, RBI Mumbai.
Online fraud: also 1930 immediately.

entries.title: Stock broker, demat, mutual fund, listed company investor grievance
entries.who: The company/broker first; then SEBI SCORES; then SMART ODR; appeals to the Securities Appellate Tribunal.

channels.name: SEBI SCORES
channels.how: File with PAN; the complaint auto-routes to the entity; broker resolution clock is 21 days.

channels.name: SMART ODR (conciliation then arbitration)
channels.how: For unresolved disputes; filing it while a SCORES complaint is pending closes the SCORES complaint.

escalation: Complain to the broker/company compliance officer.
SCORES; if unhappy request a review within 15 days of closure.
SMART ODR.
Securities Appellate Tribunal for SEBI orders.

sources.t: RTI Wiki: SCORES 2026 and SMART ODR

entries.title: Voter ID, electoral roll, election-code violation, polling issues
entries.who: Electoral Registration Officer / District Election Officer / Chief Electoral Officer, Maharashtra; Election Commission of India.

channels.name: Voter Helpline
channels.how: Queries, complaints, status of applications.

channels.name: cVIGIL app
channels.how: Report model-code/expenditure violations with photo/video during an election period; target action within 100 minutes.

channels.name: Voter Helpline app / ECI grievance portal (NGSP)
channels.how: Roll corrections, complaints and tracking.

sources.t: Citizen Matters: voter helplines and apps

entries.title: Builder / real-estate: delayed possession, refund, carpet-area, misleading promises (MahaRERA)
entries.who: Maharashtra Real Estate Regulatory Authority (MahaRERA) for registered projects.

channels.name: MahaRERA complaint
channels.how: Register on the portal, file the complaint against the promoter with documents, pay the prescribed fee (commonly cited ₹5,000; verify on portal), track by acknowledgement number.

escalation: Legal notice to builder.
MahaRERA complaint / conciliation.
Appeal to Maharashtra Real Estate Appellate Tribunal.
Consumer Commission is also available for deficiency in service.

entries.title: Railway complaints: train, station, food, cleanliness, staff
entries.who: Indian Railways via RailMadad; zonal Railway Public Grievance cell.

channels.name: RailMadad
channels.how: Give PNR/journey details; complaints from any channel are logged here.

escalation: Zonal Railway PG cell (Central / Western Railway for Mumbai-Thane).
CPGRAMS pgportal.gov.in (Ministry of Railways).
Consumer Commission for loss/deficiency.

entries.title: Mobile / broadband / DTH complaint, spam calls, billing
entries.who: Your service provider's two-tier grievance mechanism (TRAI rules); then DoT Public Grievance cell.

channels.name: Provider complaint centre, then appellate authority
channels.how: Get a docket number; the provider must resolve within the TRAI time limits.

channels.name: DoT Public Grievance cell
channels.how: Escalate with proof the provider failed.

escalation: Provider complaint centre → Appellate Authority → DoT PG cell / CPGRAMS → Consumer Commission.

entries.title: Emergency and safety helplines
entries.who: 112 is the unified emergency number.

channels.name: Emergency numbers
channels.how: 112 all emergencies; 100 police; 108 ambulance; 101 fire; 1091 women helpline; 1098 child helpline; 14567 senior citizens; 1930 cyber fraud.

entries.title: Your rights as a citizen of India
entries.who: Enforceable through courts (Article 32 Supreme Court, Article 226 High Court) and statutory bodies.

channels.name: Free legal aid
channels.how: Free legal services via the District Legal Services Authority / NALSA for eligible persons (women, children, SC/ST, persons in custody, low income).

rightsList: Article 14: equality before law; Article 15: no discrimination; Article 16: equal opportunity in public jobs.
Article 19: speech, peaceful assembly, association, movement, profession (reasonable restrictions apply).
Article 21: life and personal liberty; includes privacy, dignity, speedy trial, clean environment. Article 21A: education 6-14.
Article 22: on arrest you must be told the grounds, can consult a lawyer, and must be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours.
Article 32 / 226: move the Supreme Court / High Court for enforcement of rights. Article 300A: property cannot be taken without law.
RTI Act 2005: right to information. Consumer Protection Act 2019: six consumer rights. Maharashtra Right to Public Services Act 2015: services within a time limit.
BNSS: free FIR copy, Zero FIR, arrest memo and right to inform a relative; women cannot ordinarily be arrested after sunset and before sunrise without magistrate order.

entries.title: Unsafe or contaminated food: rat/insect/hair in food, stale or expired food, food poisoning, adulteration
entries.who: FSSAI sets the rules; the state Food Safety Officers (Maharashtra FDA) inspect, sample and prosecute. For delivery apps, the platform and the restaurant are also answerable.

channels.name: FSSAI grievance portal
channels.how: Register the complaint with photos, bill, place and date (the Food Safety Connect app exists but is reported to be unreliable, so use the portal).

channels.name: Maharashtra FDA (Food & Drug Administration)
channels.how: Complain to the FDA for the district: the Food Safety Officer can inspect and seal the premises. Online complaint portal plus district offices.

channels.name: Compensation / refund
channels.how: Complain to the restaurant or app first (keep chat/email), then National Consumer Helpline.

entries.evidence: Do not discard the food: photograph/video it with the bill, packaging and the premises, and keep a sealed sample if safe. If anyone fell ill, get medical care first and keep prescriptions and bills.
escalation: Restaurant / delivery app written complaint.
FSSAI portal and Maharashtra FDA.
NCH 1915, then District Consumer Commission for compensation (illness, medical costs).
Serious harm: also inform the local police (negligence is a criminal offence).

sources.t: Restaurant India: food hygiene complaints on Maharashtra FDA portal

entries.title: Bribe demanded by a government employee or police officer (Maharashtra)
entries.who: Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) Maharashtra investigates bribe demands by state government employees, including police and traffic police, in every district (Mumbai, Thane, Pune, etc.). Central government employees: CBI / CVC.

channels.name: ACB Maharashtra toll-free helpline
channels.how: Report the demand; the ACB can verify and lay a trap. Do not pay first.

channels.name: ACB WhatsApp / website
channels.how: Send details of the officer, office, amount asked and date.

entries.evidence: Name/designation/badge or vehicle number of the officer, place, date and time, amount asked, any call recording or message. Complain before paying.
escalation: For a traffic cop: also email the traffic HQ / DCP Traffic of that city with the same details.
ACB divisional office of your district.
Department vigilance cell / Lokayukta Maharashtra.
Central employees: CVC (cvc.gov.in) or CBI.

channels.name: Danger or crime in progress
channels.how: Call first.

channels.how: Aaple Sarkar grievance portal with a token; reopen to escalate.

channels.name: Central government body
channels.how: CPGRAMS grievance portal.

channels.name: Shop, company or service (refund, defect)
channels.how: National Consumer Helpline.

channels.name: Bribe demanded
channels.how: Anti-Corruption Bureau Maharashtra.

channels.name: Free legal help
channels.how: District Legal Services Authority / NALSA.
